Something is already using VexLife's background service on this Mac, but VexLife does not have enough matching evidence to stop it automatically. To protect your data it will not guess. If you already have a Vex Home somewhere else, choose that location. If another VexLife is open, quit it and choose Check Again. If you believe this is a stale VexLife service, inspect the exact job in Terminal with `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.vexlife.prod.service`. If that output identifies the VexLife service you expect, you can explicitly remove that job with `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.vexlife.prod.service`, then reopen VexLife. Do not kill Python or Java processes broadly.
